metadata.case_name: LAW SZE CHUN v. LI MIE CHUN

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to the left knee
source: Both experts diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from soft tissue injury to the left knee.
On examination, it was found that her left knee was swollen with tenderness, abrasion and bruises over it. X-ray of her left knee was unremarkable.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of knee or lower leg

manifestations.description: abrasion and bruises over left knee
reduced range of movement of the left knee, limited by pain
residual pain in left knee, particularly on exertion (prolonged walking, squatting, walking up and down stairs)
cannot walk tip-toe or squat or perform single leg stand with left leg
walks in a slow pace with foot dragging
needed a wheelchair for the first 6 months after the accident
difficulty climbing 5 floors of stairs (affecting ability to go out for follow-ups and treatments)

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Accident and Emergency department, treated and discharged and referred to Emergency follow-up clinic
source: The plaintiff was attended by the Department of Accident and Emergency of Queen Elizabeth Hospital ("QEH"). On examination, it was found that her left knee was swollen with tenderness, abrasion and bruises over it. X-ray of her left knee was unremarkable. She was treated, discharged and referred to QEH’s Emergency follow-up clinic.

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at QEH Emergency follow-up clinic until 25 April 2014; continuous sick leave given by them until 8 May 2014
source: She was attended to there until 25 April 2014, with continuous sick leave given by them until 8 May 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (29 sessions) from 10 December 2013 until discharge on 29 April 2014
source: The plaintiff was referred to and began physiotherapy on 10 December 2013. She dutifully attended a total of 29 sessions without fail until she was discharged on 29 April 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: pain killers and use of pain relief tapes (as needed)
source: In her oral evidence which I accept, she says she often needs pain killers and has to put on pain relief tapes around her left knee.

treatments_future.treatment: future medical expenses to cater for pain on a need basis
source: The plaintiff claims, and in the circumstances I think it reasonable to award, future medical expenses to cater for this pain on a need basis.

losses.description: For the first 6 months after the accident she could not walk and had to be wheel-chaired; afterwards she can walk only very slowly and not for long; cannot squat; pain and weakness on exertion; difficulty climbing stairs

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Tasks of purchasing ingredients for making meals and other shopping previously performed by the plaintiff are now taken care of by her son
She now hardly goes out alone and cannot enjoy going to the market or occasionally going to the park as before
